Pairs of genomes with a known true relationship, and their IBD

Source: R/segments.R
ibd_truth_pairs.Rd

Assembles pairs whose relationship is known from the event log – a genome with itself, clonal founder copies, a relapse against the hypnozoite batch it activated from, the same lineage in two hosts, siblings co-transmitted from one oocyst, and distinct founder lineages – and attaches the ground-truth IBD of each. Feed it to plot_relatedness_ladder() to check the genealogy against the textbook values.

Usage

ibd_truth_pairs(run, max_per_class = 60)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

max_per_class

the most pairs per relationship class, the first the event log gives.

Value

a data.table of cls (a factor of the six classes), a and b (integer pedigree ids) and ibd (double), one row per pair. A class with no pair in the run has no rows, and a run with none, such as one that never started, gives a table with no rows.

Python

The IBD and ARG functions read a run's tree sequence with Python's tskit, through the reticulate package. Either of two routes works. Automatic: with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy the first time one of these functions runs; this needs internet once. Your own Python: set RETICULATE_PYTHON to a Python that has those modules (in ~/.Renviron to keep it) before the first such call of a session. A function that cannot reach them stops with an error of class malariafwd_no_python that says what to do, and check_setup() reports what is found.

Examples

tp <- ibd_truth_pairs(example_run())
tp[, .(pairs = .N, mean_ibd = mean(ibd)), by = cls]
#>                      cls pairs  mean_ibd
#>                   <fctr> <int>     <num>
#> 1:    self (same genome)    20 1.0000000
#> 2:         clonal copies     4 1.0000000
#> 3: relapse vs its origin    60 1.0000000
#> 4: same lineage, 2 hosts    12 1.0000000
#> 5:      same-oocyst sibs     8 0.3680145
#> 6:     distinct founders    45 0.0000000
